questions.question: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 22, 30, 20, 32, 18, ?
questions.questionHtml:
Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series.

22, 30, 20, 32, 18, ?
questions.solution:
The series has two alternate patterns:

Odd positions:
22, 20, 18 → decreasing by 2

Even positions:
30, 32, ? → increasing by 2

So,
32 + 2 = 34

Answer: (c) 34

questions.question: If the month of October 2025 started on Thursday, then which date will be the last Thursday of April 2026?
questions.questionHtml: If the month of October 2025 started on Thursday, then which date will be the last Thursday of April 2026?
questions.solution:
October = 31 days
November = 30 days
December = 31 days
January = 31 days
February = 28 days
March = 31 days

Total = 31 + 30 + 31 + 31 + 28 + 31 = 182 days

So, 1 April 2026 will also be Thursday.

Therefore, Thursdays in April 2026 are:

1, 8, 15, 22, 29

So, the last Thursday of April 2026 = 29.

questions.question: 40 is related to 64 following certain logic. Following the same logic, 30 is related to 36. To which of the following numbers is 65 related, following the same logic?
questions.questionHtml: 40 is related to 64 following certain logic. Following the same logic, 30 is related to 36. To which of the following numbers is 65 related, following the same logic?
questions.solution:
Logic:
Divide the number by 5, then square the result.

Check:
40 ÷ 5 = 8
8² = 64

30 ÷ 5 = 6
6² = 36

Now,
65 ÷ 5 = 13
13² = 169

Answer: (c) 169

questions.question: If in a certain code language, ALMIRAH is written as CNOKTCJ , then how will CLOSET be written in that code language?
questions.questionHtml: If in a certain code language, ALMIRAH is written as CNOKTCJ , then how will CLOSET be written in that code language?
questions.solution:
Logic:
Each letter is moved 2 steps forward in the alphabet.

ALMIRAH → CNOKTCJ

A + 2 = C
L + 2 = N
M + 2 = O
I + 2 = K
R + 2 = T
A + 2 = C
H + 2 = J

Now apply the same logic to CLOSET:

C + 2 = E
L + 2 = N
O + 2 = Q
S + 2 = U
E + 2 = G
T + 2 = V

So,

CLOSET → ENQUGV

Answer: (c) ENQUGV

questions.question: Below are three statements, followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from the statements. Statements: Some grasshoppers are green creatures. All green creatures are amphibians. Some amphibians are reptiles. Conclusions: I. Some amphibians are grasshoppers. II. Some green creatures are reptiles.
questions.questionHtml:
Below are three statements, followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from the statements.

Statements:
Some grasshoppers are green creatures.
All green creatures are amphibians.
Some amphibians are reptiles.

Conclusions:
I. Some amphibians are grasshoppers.
II. Some green creatures are reptiles.
questions.solution:
Statements:

From (1) and (2):
Some grasshoppers are amphibians.
So, Conclusion I follows.

For Conclusion II:
We only know that some amphibians are reptiles, but it is not necessary that those amphibians are green creatures.
So, Conclusion II does not follow.

Answer: Only I follows.
